name: Berodach-baladan
overview: Berodach-baladan was a male king of Babylon, as identified in 2 Kings 20:12. The Scriptures present him as a historical ruler without additional tribal or personal notes. His role as king places him within the political context of the ancient Near East during the time of the Israelite monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Berodach-baladan appears as a proper name in 2 Kings 20:12, with no specific meaning provided. He is also referred to by the title 'King of Babylon,' which literally means 'king of Babel,' indicating his royal authority over Babylon. Additionally, the variant name Merodach-baladan is found in Isaiah 39:1, showing a slight variation in spelling but referring to the same individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Berodach-baladan was the son of Baladan, as explicitly stated in 2 Kings 20:12. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Berodach-baladan's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his position as king of Babylon during a critical period in Israel's history. His reign is noted in the context of interactions with the kingdom of Judah, highlighting the geopolitical tensions of the era. Although details are limited, his mention in the Scriptures underscores the broader theme of God's sovereignty over earthly rulers and kingdoms.
